items.title: After hours of negotiations, second round of govt-opposition talks ends in a 'deadlock'
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Hours-long negotiations between the government and the opposition during a second round of talks ended in a “deadlock” early on Sunday. The meeting at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. Details on the negotiating process were sparse as both sides seemingly agreed not to speak to the media before matters concluded. However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not succeeded in a breakthrough. “Deadlock,” he told reporters waiting at Parliament House in footage aired on Geo News . Asked what the points of contention were, he said they were “small things”. He added that the “issue” of meetings with PTI founder Imran Khan could not be solved. He went on to say that the deadlock was over Imran’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He said that talks had now ended, adding that a detailed press conference would be held later. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the government’s delegation in the talks, said the talks failed primarily because the “KP government could not assure whether they would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the future”. He alleged that the PTI’s provincial government in KP did not want to implement the National Action Plan and that the PTI delegation that participated in the talks had also left the venue “disappointed because the KP government did not cooperate on terrorism”. An agreement had been reached on all other matters, he said in response to a question. Asked about the possible future course of action, he said the “Constitution has several options”, seemingly a referring to the possibility of imposing governor’s rule or emergency in KP. Separately, PPP’s Sherry Rehman, who also participated in the talks, said the government delegation debated all points with the opposition. “Unfortunately, the draft [agreement] was changed four times after it was agreed upon,” she told Geo News , adding that she would not go into the details. Speaking to reporters, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said that the party’s long march was “intact” and would go ahead. At the same time, he asserted that imposing an emergency or governor rule was not the answer to the protest. He further said that the participants had also not reached an agreement on when the next round of talks would take place. He said that the opposition’s demands presented during the second round of talks were “simple” and included meetings with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi. He said that there were a few issues pertaining to terrorism, where the negotiating process became “stuck”. Hours-long talks Visuals broadcast by DawnNewsTV after 9:30pm showed Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi — part of the government delegation — departing Parliament House with a document in his hand, with media reports suggesting he was likely to consult the president. More than an hour later, footage showed Naqvi returning to Parliament House, with the interior minister maintaining his silence as reporters swarmed him for queries. The meeting, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. The PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march , aimed at demanding Imran’s release, has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government. Even as extended talks kept hopes for an agreement alive, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi remained adamant on proceeding with PTI’s march to Islamabad. After voicing his determination on Saturday afternoon — which irked government representatives — the KP CM again took to X at 12:46am to detail the itinerary for the protest march. Laying out the journey plan, Afridi said PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan, Bannu, and Lakki Marwat will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4. The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat. Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani. The KP CM’s post went on to say that the caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange.” They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them. Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.” NA speaker hopes for ‘cordial’ talks When the huddle began, the NA speaker expressed his hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as Friday’s, according to a post on the NA’s X account. The government side included Naqvi, Tallal Minister for States and Frontier Regions Amir Muqam, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah. Rehman, along with MNAs Syed Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Hussain Jakhrani, represented the PPP. The opposition delegation comprised the Senate opposition leader, PTI interim chairman Gohar Ali Khan, Opposition Chief Whip Amir Dogar, MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh. Prior to the meeting with the government, the opposition held a meeting in which standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the talks were finalised. It was decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one from either side would speak to the media during the talks and that a joint statement would be issued afterwards to avoid any misunderstanding. Speaking to Dawn , TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai said comments made by PPP’s Rehman on Friday had triggered a controversy, leaving the situation unpleasant until late at night. “The opposition alliance held a meeting before the start of the talks, during which the government side’s views regarding the law and order situation in KP were discussed. After consultation with the KP chief minister, a response was prepared, which will be presented to the government side during the meeting today,” he said. For the first time in almost three years, representatives of the federal government and the opposition PTI formally came together on Friday for talks aimed at easing the political tension in the country, and apprised each other of their positions. Though neither side had shared its specific demands with the media, both were hopeful of a positive outcome from the meeting. Sources on both sides told Dawn that the PTI wants Imran to be shifted from jail to a hospital for medical treatment, while the government has insisted that the opposition call off its protest march on Islamabad. In August, PTI announced a long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4. Tariq Fazal objects to KP CM’s remarks CM Afridi’s Saturday statement vowed to hold the long march on Oct 4 and to prevent a repeat of the events of May 9, 2023. He said PTI was the largest and most popular political party in Pakistan. “Pakistan is a democratic country whose Constitution grants us the right to peaceful protest.” Detailing his long march plan, Afridi said an “ocean of people” would begin its journey from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4. The party would continue its struggle until the supremacy of the Constitution and the law was ensured in Pakistan and an independent judiciary was restored, the PTI leader added. “All demands of the PTI are in accordance with the constitution and the law.” He stressed that the party would “neither allow May 9 to happen again nor allow anyone else to repeat it”. Reacting to the KP CM’s remarks, Chaudhry said Afridi’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process even though the government wanted them to be “meaningful and fruitful”. He urged PTI leaders to refrain from making such statements until the final stage of the negotiations, so that the dialogue process was not “harmed”. “The language that Sohail Afridi is using against his opponents and our leadership does not seem like that of a chief minister; his statements are extremely indecent and reprehensible,” Chaudhry said. Speaking to reporters ahead of the meeting, PPP’s Rehman stressed that her party was making efforts to solve issues in a democratic manner. Asked about KP CM being adamant on the PTI march, the PPP leader said it was up to the PTI, but added that she would refrain from making comments before the talks conclude. While acknowledging that each party had its positions, she noted that the objective of holding negotiations was to “discuss those positions”. ‘Political solutions to political problems’ Separately, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, an ally of the PML-N government, reiterated his call for PTI to call off its long march. Speaking at an event in Karachi on Saturday, Bilawal said it was his party that urged the Centre to engage in dialogue with PTI whereas the federal government had “made up its mind” on imposing emergency or governor’s rule in KP. In a post on X on Friday, the PPP chairman had pressed PTI to unconditionally call off the long march, which he said would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and threats emanating from neighbouring countries. Bilawal also welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”. Also on Friday, the army’s top brass warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”. Ahead of the talks, federal ministers had warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI had warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken. The decision to hold talks was taken on Thursday at a presidency meeting attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Naqvi, Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan and other PPP and PML-N leaders. A source privy to the huddle told Dawn the emergency option was discussed, but participants agreed to first give the opposition a chance to settle matters peacefully through dialogue, and to seriously consider an emergency only if the PTI did not back down. The coalition also believes the march will remain confined to KP and not enter Punjab or Islamabad. On Thursday, Sanaullah said the government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” over the protest, and that the decision on the march rested with the PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”. “So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned. Separately, PM Shehbaz has invited NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai for dialogue, and the two are expected to meet in the coming days.

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE MAKING OF HAMAS
items.description: During the 1970s and 1980s, a dramatic political shift permanently altered the geopolitical topography of the Middle East and the broader Muslim world. Islamism gained momentum as secular nationalism declined. It was a collapse accelerated by the defeat of Egypt, Syria and Jordan in the 1967 Arab-Israeli War. At the time, Western powers viewed Islamism, a right-wing ideology opposed to socialism and secular nationalism, as a useful counterweight to Soviet-backed nationalist regimes in Egypt, Syria, Iraq and, later, Libya. One of the most consequential applications of this strategy unfolded in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Gaza. Anti-Israel Palestinian resistance was largely dominated by secular and left-leaning groups operating primarily within the Israeli-occupied territories of Palestine and neighbouring nationalist Arab states. The French scholar Jean-Pierre Filiu wrote that, in order to neutralise Palestinian resistance groups, Israel quietly nurtured the growth of local Islamist movements, specifically the Palestinian branch of the Muslim Brotherhood. This was a deliberate strategy, designed to fragment and undermine the primary face of Palestinian nationalism: Yasser Arafat’s left-leaning and secular Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO). For Israeli strategists, the PLO’s anti-colonial rhetoric posed a serious political threat. To curb the PLO’s influence, Israeli military intelligence began to cultivate a counterweight in the shape of Sheikh Ahmed Yassin. A charismatic Palestinian cleric, Yassin had begun building a social and religious network under the Muslim Brotherhood umbrella in Gaza, culminating in the founding of al-Mujama al-Islami in 1973. The PLO viewed Yassin’s followers as “quietist fundamentalists” preoccupied with social welfare and moral purification. The PLO did not exhibit concern even when Israeli authorities permitted al-Mujama to operate unhindered. In 1979, the Israeli military administration formally recognised the al-Mujama charity, granting it permission to establish mosques, schools and medical clinics across Gaza. Israel’s relentless efforts, across decades, to weaken secular Palestinian resistance to its occupation of Palestine by backing a ‘counterweight’ ultimately backfired. The current Hamas is the blowback According to Filiu, while PLO sympathisers faced relentless crackdowns, Yassin was allowed to build a vast social network. Gulf funds, primarily from Saudi Arabia, flowed into al-Mujama’s coffers with minimal Israeli interference. In 1978, Israeli authorities even permitted the establishment of an Islamic university in Gaza, which eventually became a stronghold for Islamist recruitment. Years later, Brig Gen Yitzhak Segev, the Israeli military governor of Gaza in the late 1970s and early 1980s, admitted that he was provided a state budget to assist in funding Yassin’s project to offset the PLO. In the book Israel’s Wars, political scientist Ahron Bregman wrote that defence minister Yitzhak Rabin maintained a policy throughout the 1980s of tolerating Yassin and his organisation’s activities, provided their hostility remained directed at the PLO rather than Israeli soldiers. Illustration by Abro The late 1970s and early 1980s saw violent clashes erupt across Gaza and the West Bank between the PLO and Yassin’s followers. Members and supporters of al-Mujama torched PLO offices, attacked cinemas and targeted secular intellectuals. However, the assumption that Yassin’s movement would remain a benign social organisation focused solely on rivalling the PLO proved to be a miscalculation. Writing in The Wall Street Journal in 2009, journalist Andrew Higgins documented how Israeli forces raided Yassin’s home in 1984 following a tip-off, discovering a concealed weapons cache. Yassin was arrested and sentenced to 12 years in prison. Yet, Higgins added, in a move underscoring Israel’s persistent conviction that Islamists remained a secondary threat compared to secular nationalists, Israel released Yassin just 11 months later, in 1985. The turning point occurred in December 1987 with the outbreak of the first Intifada, a spontaneous grassroots uprising against Israeli occupation. Fearing that the PLO would bounce back to take command of the uprising, Yassin and his inner circle transformed al-Mujama al-Islami into a militant resistance organisation. In early 1988, the group published its founding covenant under a new name: Hamas. Hamas was thus the direct byproduct of a charitable and proselytising network shaped in the 1970s by the Gaza chapter of the Muslim Brotherhood and facilitated by Israeli policy. Its original objective of drawing Palestinians toward religious piety and discrediting secular groups, evolved during the Intifada into an armed struggle. Hamas’ 1988 charter combined militant anti-Zionism with unyielding Islamism, calling for an Islamic state in Palestine and rejecting the PLO’s gradual move toward a diplomatic, two-state compromise. Even during the initial months of the Intifada, Israeli authorities hesitated to suppress Hamas with the severity applied to the PLO, hoping the group would fracture the uprising. However, as Higgins observed, when Hamas initiated armed attacks, kidnappings and suicide operations against Israeli personnel, Tel Aviv recognised the scale of its strategic error. By the time Israel outlawed Hamas and rearrested Yassin in 1989, the network that Israel helped nurture was deeply entrenched. This manoeuvre yielded a fierce adversary. Much like the American backing of the Afghan mujahideen in the 1980s, Israel’s policy towards the Palestinian Muslim Brotherhood became a classic instance of strategic blowback. A quietist religious charity group transformed into an entrenched militant movement. Even after the PLO’s influence waned from the 1990s onwards, evidence indicates that Israel’s strategic interest in leveraging Hamas persisted. As reported by The New York Times and The Times of Israel in 2023, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition governments facilitated hundreds of millions of dollars in Qatari cash transfers into Gaza between 2009 and 2023. The objective was to keep Hamas viable in Gaza, thereby keeping the Palestinian leadership permanently divided and isolating the PLO in the West Bank. Netanyahu explicitly articulated this doctrine during his party’s meeting in March 2019, stating: “Anyone who wants to thwart the establishment of a Palestinian state has to support bolstering Hamas…” This was widely quoted by major Israeli newspapers. This policy relied on tactical coordination, work-permit allocations and economic incentives to manage Hamas, while derailing two-state diplomatic efforts. As detailed in one of Israel’s largest newspapers, Haaretz, in 2023, this long-standing gamble to sustain Hamas as a political wedge ultimately collapsed with the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023. In the aftermath, some analysts argued that the far-right Israeli administration intentionally overlooked intelligence warnings to allow an attack that could serve as a pretext for destroying Gaza and dismantling opposition in the West Bank. In November 2023, The New York Times reporters Ronen Bergman and Adam Goldman revealed that Israeli military and intelligence agencies had possessed a detailed, 40-page Hamas attack plan for over a year. This may be a show of reckless indifference, or an exhibition of hubris and a flawed strategic doctrine that assumed Hamas was permanently deterred. Indeed, but there is an increasing number of analysts who view the failure to act on these blueprints as evidence of deliberate omission. Published in Dawn, EOS, October 4th, 2026

items.title: Onus on state to protect kids from online harm, IHC told
items.description: • NCRC recommends boosting NCCIA capacity, setting up special units for exploitation probes • Proposes Peca review from child rights perspective • Urges integrating age verification into Digital Nation Pakistan Act ISLAMABAD: Protecting minors from online grooming, exploitation and harmful content is the state’s responsibility, the National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC) told the Islamabad High Court while proposing sweeping legal and institutional reforms to safeguard children on social media. In a 17-page response submitted to the court in a case concerning social media usage by children under the age of 16, the commission acknowledged the concerns raised in the petition. It underscored the need for age verification mechanisms and a comprehensive regulatory framework, stating that effective legal and regulatory measures are indispensable for online child safety. The NCRC recommended integrating child online safety into the regulatory framework of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act, with a focus on age verification and effective protection systems. To combat technology-facilitated child exploitation, the commission recommended boosting the capacity of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency and establishing specialised systems to investigate online child sexual exploitation. The commission also recommended a review and amendment of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the context of child rights, noting the need to improve the existing legal framework for online child safety. Digital platforms must be made more accountable for child safety, the commission said. It urged effective action against child sexual abuse material and online grooming, while implementing measures for the immediate removal of such content. “There is also a need to limit unnecessary online contact between children and unknown adults,” the commission said, adding that legislation, platform accountability and effective enforcement are essential for children’s online safety. The NCRC noted the importance of striking an effective balance between children’s digital rights and their protection online. The commission asserted that the issue of children’s online safety demands effective legal and institutional measures rather than mere policy. Advocates Muhammad Jalal Haider and Yahya Farid are representing the petitioner in the case. Published in Dawn, October 4th, 2026

items.title: Son jailed for threatening to stab mother
items.description: The Tarkwa Circuit Court has sentenced Joseph Quaye, a 26-year-old unemployed man, who threatened to stab his mother with a knife and a pair of scissors, to four years’ imprisonment in hard labour. He pleaded guilty to threat of death and was convicted on his own plea by the presiding judge, Bernice Mensima Ackon. Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Veronica Tibson, who led prosecution, told the court that, the complainant Afua Adenzie is a trader, mother of Quaye, and a resident of Ningo, a town near Benso in the Western Region. She said Quaye had been having issues with the mother for some time and had repeatedly threatened to assault her. She said around 7:00 pm, on June 12, 2026, the complainant was at her residence in Ningo when Quaye walked in. ASP Tibson stated that the complainant perceived an offensive odour coming from Quaye and advised him to bathe properly. The prosecutor said Quaye became angry, quarrelled with the complainant and insulted her, calling her a prostitute, smelling mouth and other provocative words. Quaye then pulled a pair of scissors from his pocket and threatened to stab the complainant, but she pleaded for her life. ASP Tibson said that, at about 2:00 am, on June 13, 2026, Quaye returned to the house while the complainant and other siblings were sleeping and threatened her with a knife. The prosecution said Quaye added that if he had a gun, he would have shot the complainant in the ribs in the presence of the senior brother, who witnessed the incident. She said Quaye was picked up at the Benso police station in connection with a stolen gun issue, and the complainant, on hearing of his arrest, went to the police station and filed a complaint.

items.title: Mohamed Joudar mandaté pour conduire les négociations de l’Union constitutionnelle
items.description: Le bureau politique de l’Union constitutionnelle (UC) a décidé, à l’unanimité de ses membres, de mandater le secrétaire général du parti, Mohamed Joudar, pour conduire les consultations avec la Cheffe du gouvernement désignée et chargée de former le nouvel Exécutif, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Le bureau politique a également décidé d’accorder au secrétaire général les pleins pouvoirs pour prendre les décisions qu’il jugera appropriées, de manière à préserver la place du parti et à servir l’intérêt supérieur de la Nation. Dans un communiqué publié à l’issue de la réunion de son bureau politique, tenue samedi à Casablanca en présence de ses députés élus lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre 2026, l'UC a affirmé son « engagement positif dans le processus des consultations ». Il a précisé que sa position pour la prochaine étape sera déterminée par la convergence des programmes et la capacité à répondre aux attentes des citoyens, notamment en matière de préservation du pouvoir d'achat, d’emploi et de renforcement de l'État social. Le bureau politique a souligné que les résultats obtenus par l’Union constitutionnelle « témoignent de la présence constante du parti dans le paysage politique national », notant que l'ambition de l'UC « demeure plus grande, à la hauteur de son histoire et de son capital militant ». Le parti a appelé ses militants à redoubler d’efforts et à renforcer leur proximité avec les citoyens, en préparation des prochaines échéances électorales. Après avoir salué la mobilisation des structures du parti et de ses militants durant la campagne électorale, le bureau politique de l’UC a appelé à tirer parti de cette dynamique afin de renforcer l’organisation du parti et d’élargir sa base. The post Mohamed Joudar mandaté pour conduire les négociations de l’Union constitutionnelle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Explosions rock Sanaa as Saudi airstrikes target Houthi positions
items.description: Loud explosions rocked Yemen's Houthi-held capital Sanaa late Saturday as the Houthi-run al-Masirah TV reported renewed Saudi airstrikes on the city. A Sanaa resident, speaking to Xinhua on condition of anonymity, said warplanes could be heard overhead as powerful blasts echoed across the capital, rattling windows and shaking buildings. "The blasts were so powerful that the ground shook beneath us," the resident said. "It felt like an earthquake. Our windows were rattling, and the children woke up terrified." Residents believe that the airstrikes targeted Houthi positions. Casualties were not immediately known. Earlier on Saturday, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital Riyadh in retaliation for what they described as intensified Saudi strikes on Yemen. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said that 60 air and missile strikes had hit Yemen over the previous 24 hours. After the exchange of strikes between Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Yemen's armed forces said ‌early on Sunday it was conducting strikes against the Houthis in the capital Sanaa and the group's ​stronghold Saada. A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, ​which are aligned with the internationally recognized government, said forces were targeting what he described ​as "vital targets," without providing further details. (With input from agencies)

items.title: Drive constitutional reform – GJA urges journalists
items.description: The Vice-President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Rebecca Ekpe, has urged colleague journalists to lead the charge in ensuring that Ghana’s constitutional reform is owned by Ghanaians. This, she said, called for journalists to reflect on their constitutional responsibilities and not leave the entire process to a select few. “We must scrutinise the exercise of public power and ensure that every voice is heard,” she said. The GJA vice-president said journalists should ensure that the revised Constitution represented the views of every Ghanaian. Ms Ekpe was speaking at a media engagement in Accra last Thursday by the Citizens Platform for the constitutional reforms. Platform The platform is constituted by more than 100 Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). Ms Ekpe said the media was an integral part of the conversation, without which its implementation would face challenges. In that regard, she called for inclusiveness, independence, integrity and excellence. A Senior Advisor at International IDEA, Adem Abebe, said the success of the reforms depended on the media and that role should be protected. “Indeed, the media is a powerful avenue in shaping opinions. In that regard, let’s ensure that every voice is heard,” he said. The media training was to take practitioners through the various position papers by the CSOs, the Institute of Economic Affairs, labour unions and the New Patriotic Party (NPP). The training was to seek the views of media practitioners on how to synchronise the various position papers and examine how it could affect some existing legislation.

items.title: Santé: 73 % des Marocains inquiets du coût et de l’accès aux soins
items.description: Une enquête menée par le réseau Afrobarometer révèle des tendances marquées chez les citoyens marocains concernant le financement des services publics de santé. Une large proportion des personnes interrogées se montre réticente à l’idée d’une hausse des impôts destinée à financer des soins de santé universels, alors même qu’un niveau élevé d’inquiétude personnelle est observé quant au coût des soins et à la capacité de les assumer en cas de maladie. Les résultats de l’enquête, publiée sous le titre « Payer pour les soins de santé pour tous : l’acceptation du financement à travers l’Afrique », montrent que seulement 48 % des Marocains interrogés se déclarent favorables à une augmentation des impôts en contrepartie de la garantie, par l’État, de soins de santé adéquats pour tous. Ce taux place le Maroc en avant-dernière position parmi les 38 pays africains couverts par l’étude, loin de la moyenne continentale, qui s’établit à 70 %. Contrairement à la tendance observée dans la plupart des pays d’Afrique subsaharienne, les données recueillies auprès des Marocains font apparaître une certaine proximité avec le contexte nord-africain. Le taux d’acceptation de la « proposition fiscale » est ainsi comparable à celui enregistré en Tunisie (77 % de soutien) et en Mauritanie (71 %). Il reste toutefois nettement inférieur à celui observé dans des pays comme le Gabon, le Sénégal et le Cap-Vert, où le taux de soutien dépasse 88 %. Selon la même source, cet écart s’explique par le fait que les citoyens des pays disposant déjà de systèmes de santé établis ou de chantiers en cours en matière de couverture sociale considèrent une « hausse des impôts » comme un coût supplémentaire pour des services censés déjà exister. Dans les pays dépourvus de couverture sanitaire, la proposition est davantage perçue comme l’instauration d’un service entièrement nouveau. En parallèle à cette réserve concernant la fiscalité, la même enquête montre que l’accès aux soins reste une préoccupation majeure pour les Marocains. Quelque 73 % des participants se disent ainsi « plutôt » ou « très » inquiets de ne pas pouvoir obtenir les soins médicaux nécessaires ou d’être incapables d’en supporter les coûts. Ce taux est proche de la moyenne africaine, qui s’élève à 74 %. Concernant l’expérience des citoyens avec les établissements publics de santé, 46 % des personnes ayant eu recours auparavant aux hôpitaux publics indiquent que l’accès aux services était « facile » ou « très facile ». À l’inverse, 54 % estiment que les démarches et l’accès aux soins sont difficiles. Les résultats de l’enquête Afrobarometer mettent ainsi en évidence un équilibre délicat autour de la question de « l’acceptation du financement » : les citoyens doivent concilier leur besoin important de couverture sanitaire avec leur sensibilité à l’égard d’une charge fiscale supplémentaire. L’acceptation d’un nouveau financement fiscal apparaît dès lors liée à la capacité de l’État à transformer ces ressources en services de santé concrets et de qualité dans les établissements publics. items.title: Beyond ACG: US creators behind NHS find an audience in China
items.description: What if animals were just like us? For Natural Habitat Shorts (NHS), that simple idea has grown into a global animation phenomenon, reaching audiences far beyond its American roots. The animated short-video series puts animals in familiar human situations while weaving in facts about their unusual habits. What began as a small creative project among three friends has now brought its creators to China to meet an audience they never expected to have. From a small project to a global audience The idea began in 2020. The team initially saw NHS as a creative outlet alongside their full-time jobs, hoping simply to build "a small following." They came up with a short video about animals working in a grocery store. But when some viewers failed to understand why the animals behaved in certain ways, the creators saw an opportunity to add educational elements. For example, a bat character uses echolocation, which explains why it was screaming in the video. From there, NHS developed its distinctive formula: placing animals with real-world characteristics into relatable human situations. "Everyone goes to work and deals with everyday human problems," said Nicole Low, one of the creators. "Putting animals in that situation with crazy animal habits just adds another layer of comedy." That approach may also help explain why the series has resonated across cultural boundaries. The creators say that even when American humor does not translate perfectly, emotions such as stress, jealousy and awkwardness remain relatable. "I think a lot of the humor comes from the discomfort and stress that the animals deal with," said Brennan Brinkley, one of the NHS creators. "That's kind of a universal thing." An unexpected connection with China China, in particular, turned out to be an audience they discovered almost by accident. The team began receiving messages from Chinese viewers on overseas platforms and later learned that their videos were being widely shared in China. "We were like, how are they seeing our videos?" Tyler Kula, one of the creators, recalled. This year, NHS officially opened accounts on Chinese social media platforms. The creators said they have been impressed by the enthusiasm and creativity of Chinese viewers, including fans who have sent them drawings and gifts. In mid-September, the three creators visited China and met their Chinese fans in person. The trip also sparked ideas for future stories. The team is considering featuring more Chinese animals, including red pandas and giant pandas, and incorporating their unusual traits into the humorous situations that define NHS. The creators also see China as a growing part of the animation landscape. For Brinkley, films such as Ne Zha 2 show the competitiveness of China's animation market. From short videos to bigger dreams And as NHS looks ahead, the possibilities are expanding beyond short videos. The creators said they would like to explore children's books, a feature-length animated film and even a video game. "Every once in a while, we'll show up in a place like China and realize, oh yeah, there's a bigger world out there," Kula said. "That's definitely a dream." items.title: NPP Delagates Congress: Confusion delays voting at Ashanti Region TESCON centre
items.description: Confusion broke out at the Ashanti Region TESCON polling area during the New Patriotic Party’s national delegates congress after some delegates struggled to locate their names on the Electoral Commission’s album. The development left several TESCON members waiting to cast their ballots, triggering agitation among the affected delegates who feared they could be disenfranchised. “We are voting,” they chanted. The confusion emerged about five and a half hours into the election, which began around 6 p.m. on Saturday, October 3. According to JoyNews’ Nana Yaw Gyimah, police moved in to restore order as EC officials worked to resolve the issue. Police cordoned off the area and directed the agitated delegates back into orderly queues while efforts were made to address their concerns. However, the National Coordinator of TESCON dismissed reports that the album containing the names of Ashanti Region TESCON delegates was missing. He explained that the region has 50 TESCON institutions, with representatives expected to vote at three designated polling centres labelled A, B and C. According to him, the confusion arose because some delegates initially went to the wrong polling centre and could not find their names before eventually locating them at the appropriate centre. “There is no issue. The whole TESCON album for the country, you know, they are all supposed to vote in their various regions. So Asante region has 50 TESCON institutions. “But our polling centres were three: A, B, C. So as to where exactly they were supposed to vote was the issue. They went to A and then they didn’t find their names. They came to B and they didn’t find their names and came to C to see their names. “And now they are voting. That was the only challenge. And it’s been resolved that they are voting now,” he said. The coordinator further insisted that the TESCON album had been available throughout the electoral process. “No, no, no. That’s never the case. It’s been here since morning,” he said when asked whether the album was missing. He explained that all 50 TESCON representatives from institutions in the Ashanti Region were captured on the EC’s sub-album and would be allowed to vote. “As I’m talking to you, you can see the voting processes have started. None of them will be disenfranchised. All the 50 people here, their names are captured on the EC sub-album. That is how come they’ve been allowed to be here,” he said. Police have since restored calm at the polling area, with voting continuing. Meanwhile, voting had ended at some other polling centres, where officials had begun counting ballots.

items.title: Lula campaign urges probe into US consular service suspension
items.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's campaign has asked the country's top electoral court to investigate whether the US decision to suspend consular services ahead of Sunday's presidential election was related to security concerns or constituted election interference, local media reported Saturday. The petition, filed by Lula's Brasil Pronto Pra Mais coalition with the Superior Electoral Court, argued that the suspension could have portrayed Brazil as unstable on the eve of the vote and benefited opposition candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. The US Embassy announced Thursday that consular services at the embassy and its consulates in Brazil would be suspended starting Friday, citing "security concerns" without elaborating. US citizens were advised not to visit US diplomatic facilities, while diplomatic personnel were instructed to work remotely. The petition requested an investigation into whether opposition figures had coordinated with US government officials in connection with the suspension.

items.title: L’Office du Baccalauréat met en garde contre les arnaques aux abords de ses locaux
items.description: Dans un communiqué daté du 1er octobre 2026, la direction de l’Office du Baccalauréat alerte sur des individus qui proposent de fausses « facilitations » aux abords de ses locaux, à Dakar. L'Office du Baccalauréat sonne l'alerte. Face à la multiplication des pratiques frauduleuses autour de son siège, situé à l'Université Cheikh Anta Diop, l'institution a publié un communiqué de prévention signé de son directeur, le Pr Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba Gueye. Le texte s'adresse aux candidats, aux parents et aux agents. Des démarcheurs qui monnaient des « facilitations » Selon l'Office, des personnes sans lien avec l'institution rôdent près de ses locaux. Il dénonce « la présence récurrente » d'individus qui promettent une « facilitation administrative » contre rémunération. Il parle aussi de « toute autre forme de manœuvre frauduleuse ou d'escroquerie ». Pour les candidats comme pour les familles, le risque est double : perdre de l'argent et se retrouver avec un document sans valeur. Les démarches se font en ligne La direction rappelle qu'« aucun intermédiaire n'est habilité à agir en son nom ». Diplômes, relevés de notes, duplicatas ou corrections : toutes ces démarches s'effectuent « exclusivement en ligne ». Les paiements obéissent à la même règle. Ils passent uniquement par les moyens digitaux officiels. L'Office précise qu'« aucun règlement en espèces, ni à un guichet, ni auprès d'un tiers, n'est admis ». Des sanctions possibles pour les détenteurs Le communiqué est ferme sur les conséquences. Tout paiement hors des canaux officiels est illicite et « n'ouvre aucun droit ». Les documents obtenus par falsification sont « nuls et de nul effet ». Leurs détenteurs s'exposent à des sanctions administratives, disciplinaires et pénales. Cinq réflexes pour les usagers L'Office recommande ainsi aux usagers de : s'adresser uniquement aux guichets officiels ; payer exclusivement par les canaux digitaux officiels ; décliner fermement toute sollicitation d'inconnus aux abords des locaux ; ne verser aucune somme, en espèces ou par transfert, à des personnes qui se réclament d'une « facilitation » ; signaler immédiatement aux agents de l'Office toute proposition frauduleuse dont ils seraient l'objet ou le témoin. O.B.N

items.title: Maférinya : une violente collision entre une voiture et une moto tue deux personnes
items.description: Une voiture de transport venue de Coyah a heurté une moto en face de la station d'essence de Kimara. Les deux occupants de la moto n'ont pas survécu. La route a encore fait deux victimes à Maferinyah. Vers 19 heures, un véhicule de transport en commun et une moto se sont percutés de plein fouet en face de la station d'essence de Kimara (Mangret), dans la Sous-préfecture. Les deux personnes qui se trouvaient sur la moto ont succombé. Selon les premiers éléments recueillis sur place, la voiture arrivait de Coyah au moment où la moto, elle, venait du centre-ville de Maferinyah. Les circonstances exactes du choc restent à déterminer. Des témoins oculaires indiquent que plusieurs passagers du véhicule de transport sont grièvement blessés. Aucun bilan précis n'a encore été communiqué sur leur nombre ni sur leur état. Sous la violence de l'impact, la voiture comme la moto sont totalement détruites. Ce drame relance l'inquiétude des riverains. Sur cet axe très fréquenté, où cohabitent véhicules de transport, motos-taxis et usagers venus du centre-ville, les accidents se répètent, surtout à la tombée de la nuit. Les causes de la collision demeurent inconnues. Une enquête devra établir les responsabilités, en s'intéressant notamment à la vitesse, à l'état des véhicules et à la visibilité au moment des faits.

items.title: Soludo swears in council chairmen, demands accountability
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has sworn in the newly elected 21 local government chairmen and their deputies, charging them to prioritise service delivery, accountability and responsible use of public resources. The governor urged the officials to take their oath of office seriously, review it regularly and consider displaying it in visible locations as a constant reminder of their responsibilities. “As you begin your journey, know that it is a call to serve,” Soludo told the chairmen, urging them to be their brothers’ and sisters’ keepers, which he said was in line with the agenda of the ruling All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA). He said the officials should put aside their expectations and immediately focus on the responsibilities of office. “I know that when you were applying for the job, you had all manner of aspirations, promises and expectations. Welcome to the world of reality and the clock starts ticking today. The work has already begun,” he said. Soludo also emphasised the need for the officials to account for their time in office, noting that even the minutes spent at the swearing-in ceremony had already become part of their official responsibilities. The governor noted what he described as APGA’s dominance in Anambra State over the past 20 years, saying the party’s candidates had, in the latest council election, faced little opposition in many areas. He reminded the chairmen that previous administrations had helped build the structures on which they were assuming office, urging them to leave the local government system stronger for their successors. Soludo also urged the new council leaders to embrace innovation while ensuring that their actions remained within the law. He specifically called for measures to make the local government system more sustainable, noting that the new local government laws permitted councils to pool resources for the effective management of common financial obligations. The governor advised the chairmen to study the handover notes from their predecessors and carefully assess the assets and liabilities they had inherited, given the challenges confronting the councils. The swearing-in followed the declaration of the results of the local government election conducted on August 30, 2026. items.title: La Marocaine Oulfa Chellaï établit un nouveau record national d'apnée à 71 mètres aux Championnats du monde 2026
items.description: L'apnéiste marocaine Oulfa Chellaï, 35 ans, a établi un nouveau record national féminin en poids constant bipalmes (CWTB) en atteignant 71 mètres de profondeur lors des World Apnea 2026 Depth Championships, organisés à Limassol, à Chypre. La performance a été officiellement validée comme record national marocain. Elle constitue également un nouveau record absolu de profondeur pour l'apnée féminine marocaine, il s'agit de 10 mètres de plus par rapport aux 61 m d'août. Originaire de Marrakech, Oulfa Chellaï est physicienne au Swiss Plasma Center de l'École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), où elle travaille sur la physique des plasmas et le tokamak TCV. Son parcours conjugue ainsi recherche scientifique de haut niveau et sport de haut niveau. Une saison 2026 marquée par une progression exceptionnelle En mai, lors d'une compétition internationale à Sharm el-Sheikh, elle avait déjà établi des records marocains dans trois disciplines de profondeur : CWTB (poids constant bipalmes), CWT (poids constant avec palmes) et FIM (immersion libre). En août, aux Championnats du monde CMAS d'apnée en profondeur à Roatán, au Honduras, Oulfa Chellaï avait porté le record absolu de profondeur de l'apnée féminine marocaine à 61 mètres en CWTB. Quelques semaines plus tard, à Limassol, elle le repousse à 71 mètres. La tentative a été réalisée malgré la casse d'une palme pendant l'échauffement. À 71 mètres, sa performance correspond par ailleurs au troisième niveau de performance africain répertorié en CWTB féminin dans les classements consultés, sous réserve de leur mise à jour complète après les Mondiaux. Une plongée dédiée à Rachida Sahli Cette plongée avait aussi une dimension profondément personnelle. Oulfa Chellaï l'a dédiée à sa tante Rachida Sahli, décédée le jour de la cérémonie officielle d'ouverture des Championnats : « Je voulais emmener son sourire éternel au cœur de la mer. » Une performance qui fait franchir un cap à l'apnée féminine marocaine Membre de la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Plongée et d'Activités Subaquatiques (FRMPAS), Oulfa Chellaï contribue à installer durablement l'apnée féminine marocaine sur la scène internationale. Sa progression en 2026 illustre l'émergence d'un nouveau niveau de performance pour le Maroc dans les disciplines de profondeur. Au-delà du résultat sportif, son profil offre un récit singulier : une scientifique marocaine, originaire de Marrakech, engagée dans la recherche en physique des plasmas à l'EPFL, qui représente le Maroc au plus haut niveau international en apnée. The post La Marocaine Oulfa Chellaï établit un nouveau record national d'apnée à 71 mètres aux Championnats du monde 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: NPP Delegates conference: The wisdom of the masses will prevail – Napo
items.description: The New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) 2024 running mate, Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh, has expressed confidence in the party’s delegates to make the right choices as they vote in the party’s national executive elections. Dr Opoku Prempeh, popularly known as Napo, said the outcome of the elections should be determined by delegates, stressing that the democratic process within the party must be respected. Speaking in an interview during the NPP National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, 3 October, Dr Opoku Prempeh said he had no personal interest in influencing the outcome of the elections and was leaving the decision entirely in the hands of delegates. “The wisdom of the masses will prevail,” he said when asked about the elections being held during the conference. He said delegates from across the country had gathered to participate in an important democratic exercise that would help shape the future direction of the party. According to him, every vote cast would contribute to determining the leadership of the NPP and strengthening the party as it prepares for future elections. Dr Opoku Prempeh also commented on the NPP’s prospects ahead of the 2028 general election, acknowledging the competitive nature of elections in Ghana. “All Ghana’s elections have been tough and have been keenly contested, but at the end of the day, the wisdom of the masses will speak,” he said. He expressed confidence in the NPP’s future electoral prospects and voiced his support for Dr Mahamudu Bawumia’s political ambitions. “The voters will decide who they think will give Ghana hope from 2029 onward, and they will elect that person. And I believe sincerely, it’s going to be Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the NPP,” he said. He commended the conduct of party supporters, delegates and candidates throughout the conference, describing their participation in the internal electoral process as encouraging.

items.title: IGP deploys DIG, CPs to Imo for corps members’ rescue
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, to Imo State to coordinate the rescue of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other passengers abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway on Thursday, October 1, 2026. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Etuk, disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja. According to the statement, Nadada arrived in Imo with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing search-and-rescue operation. The statement said the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel and operational assets, and issued further directives to strengthen the coordinated response. The assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police in charge of Federal Operations, CP Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; other service commanders and members of the management team of the Imo State Police Command. The police said the search-and-rescue operation had been intensified, with additional tactical teams and operational assets deployed to identified areas, supported by intelligence-led tracking of the abductors. The statement said the police were also working closely with other security agencies to secure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and apprehend those responsible. The statement quoted Nadada as assuring the public that the Nigeria Police Force remained committed to rescuing the 20 abducted persons and would sustain the operation until its conclusion. He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant, while calling on anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to contact the police or the nearest security formation. The statement assured that all information received would be treated with strict confidentiality and that further updates would be provided as the operation progresses. items.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
items.description: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane. Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: “I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside”, which allowed the passengers in. Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. A crash axe is usually kept in the cockpit in case of an emergency. The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife. The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident. The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Multiple media outlets, including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times, have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this. While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training due to concerns about his radical views and was given another role at Oman’s national airline. He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added that he did not take any pilot training at the school. Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew, “Kill me, kill me!” The Israeli prime minister added: “So, it’s clear that he was suicidal… It looks very likely that he was going to bring the plane down.” He also said the attacker “underwent Islamist radical indoctrination”. The UAE’s attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a “terrorist act”, according to the country’s state news agency. He also said investigations were underway to establish the circumstances, motives, and any links related to the incident. Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. The pilot, who is from India, was in “good health and recovering well”, the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday. “I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again,” Machchhar said. About two and a half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport, it began to plunge sharply. The plane signalled a “general emergency” code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting “unlawful interference”, or hijacking. In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong. Almog Itali said: “Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down.” People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said. Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit. Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men – Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan – entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries. Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister’s office, that the attacker was “trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane”. Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down. He added that he “pulled the controls” of the plane. “The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there,” he said. In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster”.

items.title: Guinée : la rentrée parlementaire aura lieu ce 5 octobre
items.description: Un communiqué de l’Assemblée nationale a annoncé ce samedi 3 octobre la rentrée parlementaire prévue pour ce lundi 5 octobre à Conakry. Après plusieurs semaines de vacances parlementaires, l'institution législative s'apprête à reprendre ses travaux. Placée sous la haute autorité de Son Excellence Monsieur le Président de la République, cette rentrée marquera le coup d'envoi de l'année parlementaire. Selon le calendrier rendu public par le bureau du Parlement, les activités démarreront le lundi 5 octobre 2026 à partir de 8 heures dans la Salle des Congrès du Palais du Peuple. Les députés se retrouveront le lendemain, mardi 6 octobre, pour une série de conférences et de panels axés sur les grands enjeux de la vie parlementaire et des réformes à venir. ​L'ensemble des hauts dignitaires de la République ainsi que les corps constitués ont été conviés à prendre part à l'événement. ​Retrait des badges et présence obligatoire ​Afin d'assurer le bon déroulement de l'événement, les services de l'Assemblée nationale précisent que les badges d'accès seront disponibles et à retirer directement le lundi 5 octobre au siège de l'institution, selon les modalités prévues par le protocole. Le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Dr Dansa Kourouma, a insisté sur le caractère obligatoire de la présence de tous les honorables députés.

items.title: Labé : un militant du MODEL réagit à la grâce accordée à Aliou Bah
items.description: Dans un décret rendu public à l’occasion de la célébration du 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance de la Guinée, le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a accordé une grâce à plus de deux cents détenus. Parmi les bénéficiaires figure Aliou Bah, président du Mouvement démocratique libéral (MODEL). Interrogé sur cette décision, Aliou Dallein Baldé, militant du MODEL à Labé, se réjouit de la libération de son leader, tout en regrettant sa condamnation, qu’il qualifie d’arbitraire. Il appelle également à l’application de la décision rendue par la Cour de justice de la CEDEAO dans cette affaire. « Je suis dans un sentiment partagé entre joie et peine. La joie de savoir qu’Aliou Bah est enfin libre après vingt-deux mois de détention arbitraire. Je suis content de savoir que des enfants de moins de dix ans retrouvent leur père, qu’une épouse retrouve son mari, heureux de savoir qu’une maman puisse retrouver son enfant qui lui a été arraché arbitrairement pendant vingt-deux mois », a-t-il déclaré. Malgré cette satisfaction, le militant du MODEL dit rester préoccupé par ce qu’il considère comme les conséquences politiques de cette grâce. « Malgré que nous sommes contents de sa libération, nous sommes inquiets sur le calcul politique qui se cache derrière. Aliou Bah bénéficie d’une grâce qui peut annuler la peine, mais qui n’efface pas la condamnation. Il faut rappeler que la procédure d’Aliou Bah reste pendante à la Cour suprême. À l’état actuel, s’il sort alors qu’il n’est pas relaxé, cela va lui fermer la porte pour les élections à venir. Il ne peut être candidat avec un casier judiciaire comme ça. Il ne faudrait pas qu’il soit éliminé de la course à cause d’un casier judiciaire fabriqué », a-t-il ajouté. Aliou Dallein Baldé insiste par ailleurs sur la nécessité, selon lui, d’appliquer la décision de la Cour de justice de la CEDEAO. « La demande de la Cour de justice de la CEDEAO est de libérer le président Aliou Bah, de reconnaître que sa condamnation était arbitraire, de le dédommager à hauteur d’un franc CFA symbolique et d’effacer son casier judiciaire. La grâce présidentielle ne répond pas à cela », a-t-il souligné. Le militant du MODEL estime ainsi que la libération d’Aliou Bah constitue une étape, mais que les autres mesures évoquées dans la décision de la juridiction communautaire doivent également être prises en compte. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : un militant du MODEL réagit à la grâce accordée à Aliou Bah est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Bouré Boukaria : des dizaines de familles sans abri après de violentes inondations à Dar-Es-Salam
items.description: Une forte pluie diluvienne s’est abattue dans la nuit dernière sur la localité de Bouré Boukaria, située dans la préfecture de Kintinian, dans la région administrative de Siguiri. Cette intempérie d’une rare intensité a provoqué d’importantes inondations, frappant de plein fouet le grand quartier de Dar-Es-Salam. Le bilan matériel provisoire fait état d’au moins une trentaine d’habitations gravement touchées. Fort heureusement, aucune perte en vie humaine n’est à déplorer, mais les dégâts matériels sont considérables. Ce n’est malheureusement pas une première pour ce secteur stratégique de Bouré Boukaria. Le quartier de Dar-Es-Salam est régulièrement confronté à la récurrence de ces crues dévastatrices durant la saison des pluies. L’épisode de la nuit dernière a toutefois surpris les résidents par sa soudaineté et sa violence. L’eau a rapidement envahi les concessions, dictant sa loi et piégeant les familles dans leur sommeil. Sur le coup, plus de trente (30) habitations ont été submergées ou endommagées, plongeant la communauté dans le désarroi. Face à l’urgence de la situation, les volontaires de la Croix-Rouge locale se sont immédiatement mobilisés sur le terrain. Déployés dès les premières heures, les secouristes ont fourni des efforts remarquables pour secourir les personnes bloquées et sécuriser les sinistrés. Parallèlement aux opérations de secours, les équipes humanitaires s’activent au recensement des foyers touchés. Cette opération d’enregistrement se poursuit progressivement, secteur par secteur, afin d’établir un bilan global et précis de la catastrophe. En attendant le décompte final des services humanitaires, la situation humanitaire reste critique à Dar-Es-Salam, mais aussi à Bouré Köfilani. Privées de leurs logements inondés ou fragilisés, plusieurs familles risquent de passer cette nuit à la belle étoile, exposées aux intempéries et à l’insécurité. Les regards se tournent désormais vers les autorités locales de Boukaria, la mairie de Kintinian, ainsi que les personnes de bonne volonté, afin d’apporter une assistance humanitaire d’urgence à ces habitants régulièrement touchés. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Bouré Boukaria : des dizaines de familles sans abri après de violentes inondations à Dar-Es-Salam est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Certificats pharmaceutiques russes : le Maroc se hisse au troisième rang mondial des destinations
items.description: Avec 66 certificats de produit pharmaceutique sur 1 034 recensés depuis le 19 janvier, le Maroc se hisse au troisième rang des destinations visées par les fabricants russes. Le ministère russe de l'Industrie et du Commerce (Minpromtorg) a dénombré 1 034 certificats de produit pharmaceutique (CPP) obtenus par des fabricants russes entre le 19 janvier et le 17 septembre 2026. Sur ce total, 66 documents, soit 6,4 %, concernent le marché marocain, ce qui place le Royaume au troisième rang mondial. Seuls le Vietnam, avec 77 certificats (7,4 %), et la Mongolie, avec 73 (7,1 %), le devancent. Ces certificats attestent, devant les régulateurs des pays importateurs, que les sites de production respectent les bonnes pratiques de fabrication (GMP). Le Maroc devance ainsi ses voisins nord-africains. L'Algérie totalise 64 certificats (6,2 %) et la Libye 56 (5,4 %). Le royaume précède ainsi l'Algérie de deux certificats et la Libye de dix. À eux trois, ces marchés cumulent 186 documents, soit près de 18 % du total recensé sur la période, ce qui fait de l'Afrique du Nord la première région visée par les démarches des fabricants russes. Viennent ensuite l'Afghanistan avec 53 certificats, le Yémen (44), Cuba (40), puis les Émirats arabes unis et l'Azerbaïdjan (33 chacun). Ces données traduisent une stratégie d'homologation plutôt qu'un courant d'affaires déjà établi. En effet, un certificat ne garantit ni l'expédition de lots ni la vente de boîtes de médicaments, d'autant qu'un produit peut accumuler plusieurs enregistrements simultanés. Côté fabricants, la concentration est nette. Promomed Rus (société à responsabilité limitée) arrive en tête avec 281 certificats (27,2 %), devant Biocad (société par actions), qui en compte 126 (12,2 %), et Gueropharm, avec 123 (11,9 %). Ces trois laboratoires réunissent à eux seuls 530 documents, un peu plus de la moitié de l'ensemble (51,3 %). Promomed Rus pèse à lui seul plus d'un quart du volume total, soit davantage que Biocad et Gueropharm réunis. Loin derrière, Ozon en compte 55 (5,3 %) et Endopharm, entreprise unitaire fédérale d'État, 46 (4,4 %). Les données du Minpromtorg portent sur 321 dénominations commerciales. Le portefeuille est dominé par les traitements du diabète de type 2 et de l'obésité. Tirzetta, à base de tirzépatide, arrive en tête avec 119 certificats (11,5 %), suivie de Sedjaro, fondée sur la même molécule, avec 55 (5,3 %) : à elles deux, ces spécialités totalisent 174 certificats. Trois produits à base de sémaglutide complètent le haut du tableau : Velgia eco (40), Semavik Next (31) et Velgia (30). Les cinq premières dénominations commerciales rassemblent 275 certificats, soit 26,6 % du volume. Cette dynamique réglementaire s’inscrit dans un cadre commercial déjà substantiel entre Rabat et Moscou. L’ambassadeur de Russie au Maroc, Igor Beliaev, a récemment indiqué que les échanges bilatéraux se maintenaient entre 1,5 et 2 milliards de dollars, en citant notamment les exportations russes de produits agricoles, industriels, chimiques et pharmaceutiques vers le Royaume. Le diplomate a également fait état d’un travail visant à élargir la gamme des produits russes destinés au marché marocain, notamment à travers la certification « Halal ». The post Certificats pharmaceutiques russes : le Maroc se hisse au troisième rang mondial des destinations appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Formation du gouvernement : Ouzzine chargé de négocier au nom du Mouvement populaire
items.description: Le Conseil national du Mouvement populaire (MP) a mandaté, samedi, le secrétaire général du parti, Mohamed Ouzzine, pour poursuivre les concertations politiques et prendre la décision appropriée concernant la participation du MP au prochain gouvernement. Dans un communiqué publié à l’issue de sa session extraordinaire, le Conseil national explique que cette décision tient compte, en premier lieu, de l’intérêt supérieur de la Nation et du service des citoyens, tout en prenant en considération la responsabilité du parti, ses constantes, ses principes et ses engagements politiques. Le communiqué souligne que tout positionnement politique du parti doit permettre au Mouvement populaire de jouer un rôle influent et actif au sein des institutions, afin de défendre les préoccupations des citoyens, de contribuer à l’élaboration des politiques publiques et de traduire ses engagements envers les électeurs en positions, initiatives et programmes concrets. Le Conseil national relève également qu’en dépit du recul enregistré dans plusieurs de ses bastions électoraux traditionnels, le parti a conservé sa place sur la scène électorale nationale, estimant que ce résultat témoigne de la continuité de sa présence politique et de son ancrage institutionnel. Dans une déclaration à la presse à l’issue de cette session, le président du Conseil national du parti, Adil Sebbaï, a indiqué que la réunion a été consacrée à l’évaluation des résultats des élections législatives du 23 septembre et à l’examen de la phase politique ouverte par les concertations engagées après la nomination de la nouvelle Cheffe du gouvernement. Il a ajouté que les débats approfondis entre les membres du Conseil ont abouti à la décision de charger le secrétaire général de mener les consultations et les négociations politiques liées à cette étape. De son côté, M. Ouzzine a expliqué que cette décision est le fruit d’un débat « sincère, responsable et constructif » au sein du parlement du parti, qui a pris en considération le poids électoral et politique du Mouvement populaire. Il a également souligné que cette session a été « exceptionnelle à tous égards », tant par la participation et la mobilisation que par la nature des positions exprimées pour orienter les choix du parti durant la prochaine étape. Le SG du MP a, en outre, précisé que l’éventuelle participation du parti à la prochaine coalition gouvernementale est tributaire de conditions essentielles, dont l’intégration d’un « minimum » des engagements électoraux du MP dans le programme gouvernemental, dans le respect du contrat conclu avec les citoyens. La seconde condition, a-t-il poursuivi, concerne la prise en compte du poids politique et historique du parti ainsi que de son expérience dans l’exercice de l’action politique, aussi bien au sein de la majorité que dans les rangs de l’opposition. Tenue en présentiel et par visioconférence, cette session extraordinaire du Conseil national du Mouvement populaire a été consacrée à l’examen des résultats des élections législatives du 23 septembre et à l’analyse de leurs enseignements politiques et électoraux, ainsi qu’à l’évaluation des différentes données relatives à la prochaine étape politique. items.title: Iranian UN delegation duo ‘kicked out’ of US – State Dept
items.description: The United States has “kicked out” two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday. “Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US,” a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio “means business.” US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday. One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios. US and Iranian officials had met the week prior in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. US President Donald Trump had rejected a proposal from Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but told US media he expected talks to resume in the coming days. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported that Tehran had no more direct talks scheduled with Washington. items.title: TIDM | Le Tunisien Slim Laghmani prête serment
items.description: Le juriste et universitaire tunisien Slim Laghmani a pris officiellement ses fonctions en tant que juge au Tribunal international du droit de la mer (TIDM), lors d'une séance publique solennelle de prestation de serment. Élu lors de la 36e réunion des États à la Convention des Nations unies sur le droit de la mer, Slim Laghmani entame un mandat de neuf ans, qui a pris effet le 1er octobre 2026. Aux côtés de quatre autres nouveaux juges issus du Ghana, du Brésil, du Viet Nam et de l'Inde, il a pris l'engagement solennel d'exercer ses attributions en pleine impartialité et en toute conscience. Professeur émérite de droit public et de sciences politiques à la Faculté des sciences juridiques, politiques et sociales de Tunis, Slim Laghmani possède un parcours académique et institutionnel de premier plan. Titulaire d'un doctorat d'État et agrégé en droit public, il a dirigé le Département de droit public de Tunis et exercé comme expert juridique d'État. Acteur clé de la transition démocratique en 2011 à la tête de la sous-commission des libertés publiques, il a également représenté la Tunisie comme conseil devant la Cour internationale de Justice (CIJ) en 2024. Membre associé de l'Institut de droit international et figure de l'Académie Beït El Hikma, cette nomination au TIDM vient couronner une carrière consacrée au droit international et au droit de la mer. items.title: Benue Boat Mishap: Govt arrests boat driver, suspends maritime workers’ union
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap, with several passengers still unaccounted for . The state Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Denis Iyaghigba, ordered the immediate suspension of the union after conducting an on-the-spot assessment of the scene of the accident. The Commissioner also ordered the suspension of the line operator and directed the arrest and detention of the boat skipper involved in the mishap. The measures, according to the government, were part of immediate steps to prevent a recurrence of the incident and ensure compliance with safety regulations at the state’s waterways. The government, in a statement issued by the Head, Media and Public Orientation, Office of the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Lubem Gena, said the Ministry had activated its search and rescue operations following the accident. It said the search operation was being conducted in collaboration with local divers to intensify efforts to locate passengers who remained unaccounted for. According to the statement, “the Benue state government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap in which several passengers remain unaccounted for despite the rescue of others.” The Commissioner, who visited the scene of the incident, also directed that the line operator be suspended while the boat skipper be arrested and detained pending further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. The statement quoted Iyaghigba as saying that the government was determined to establish what led to the mishap and take measures to prevent similar incidents on the state’s waterways. “The Ministry has since activated its search and rescue processes and is working with local divers to intensify the search and rescue,” the Commissioner said. He disclosed that an inter-ministerial committee had also been constituted to investigate the incident and establish its immediate, remote and underlying causes. Iyaghigba said the committee would interrogate the circumstances surrounding the mishap and make recommendations aimed at strengthening safety standards at river crossing points across the state. He further ordered strict compliance with the mandatory use of life jackets at all river crossing points in the state. According to him, the directive was part of measures to strengthen safety and protect passengers using waterways across Benue. The Commissioner also raised concern over an abandoned barge at the crossing point which was believed to have contributed to the accident. He consequently gave the owner of the abandoned barge a seven-day ultimatum to evacuate it from the crossing point or risk having it confiscated by the state government. The statement said the Commissioner would work closely with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, during the week to further interrogate the circumstances surrounding the accident and strengthen safety measures across the state’s waterways. “The government said further details would be made available, but at the moment, investigations and rescue efforts continue,” the statement added. The latest development followed the boat mishap at the Buruku crossing point on Saturday morning where a wooden boat conveying passengers capsized while crossing the River Katsina-Ala. Several passengers were rescued following the accident, while others were reported missing, prompting the activation of search and rescue operations by the state government. items.title: Afrique : comment lutter contre la désinformation ? Dominique Tchimbakala et Le virus invisible
items.description: Une fausse information peut-elle menacer la paix d'un pays ? En Afrique, les réseaux sociaux sont devenus un terrain de circulation des rumeurs, des manipulations politiques et des campagnes de désinformation. Avec l'intelligence artificielle, le phénomène prend une nouvelle dimension. Dans Le virus invisible. Essai sur la désinformation en Afrique, publié aux éditions Riveneuve, la journaliste franco-congolaise Dominique Tchimbakala décrypte les mécanismes de la désinformation et leurs conséquences sur les sociétés africaines. Invitée du Journal de l'Afrique sur France 24, elle revient sur les responsabilités des acteurs locaux et étrangers, la défiance envers les médias et les solutions pour apprendre à reconnaître les fausses informations. Comment vérifier une information avant de la partager ? Quel rôle pour l'école, les médias et les citoyens ? Et comment lutter contre la désinformation sans menacer la liberté d'expression ? Un entretien avec Fatimata Wane.

items.title: Brain surgery in 2015 affected my penis – Julius Agwu
items.description: Nigerian comedian and actor Julius Agwu has opened up about a personal complication which followed the brain surgery he had in the United States. Agwu underwent brain surgery in 2015 after doctors reportedly discovered three tumours in his brain. One of the tumours was said to be about the size of a golf ball. Agwu disclosed that he experienced a loss of sexual function after the procedure, revealing the previously little-discussed impact during a recent episode of the Beer Parlour Talk Show uploaded on Saturday. The comedian was discussing the effects of his health battle on his body, career and personal life when the host asked if the brain condition or surgery had affected other aspects of his health, including his sexual function. Agwu responded, “After I do am, prick no dey work again now. He no dey work.” Other participants on the programme, including Mr Patrick, subsequently discussed the nerve involved in the surgery and its connection to the brain as they sought to explain the effect Agwu described. Agwu also reflected on his influence on Nigeria’s comedy industry, particularly his role in popularising the combination of music and comedy. “Music comedy na me form am o, that is to tell you how my brain dey work,” he said. The conversation later became emotional as Agwu broke down in tears while reflecting on his career, relationships and the people he felt abandoned him during his difficult period. “God wey I dey serve, anybody wey get hand for wetin happen to me. I go dey look. My friends deserted me. They stopped talking to me, many of them. It is well,” he said.
